feed.title: Kroger Makes Major Change at All Its Stores and Customers Will Notice Immediately
feed.summary: Kroger is implementing a significant change across all its stores by requiring its nearly 400,000 employees to wear new company-issued uniforms. feed.title: Biogen's experimental lupus drug shows benefit against skin symptoms
feed.summary: Biogen announced that its experimental drug, litifilimab, demonstrated durable improvement in skin symptoms for patients with cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) in a mid-stage study. The drug, which targets BDCA2 receptors to suppress inflammation, showed that 27.2% of participants achieved clear or almost clear skin after one year, with no new safety concerns identified. These results are crucial for Biogen as it seeks to diversify its product portfolio amidst challenges to its multiple sclerosis treatments.

BWXT generated $3.2 billion in revenue in 2025 and is projected to reach $3.8 billion in 2026, driven by its established business of manufacturing nuclear components for the U.S. Navy, developing advanced nuclear reactors and microreactors, and producing TRISO fuel and medical isotopes. This existing revenue and diversified involvement in the nuclear market positions BWXT for continued growth without relying solely on the successful commercialization of new reactor designs.

feed.title: Fortinet warns that critical flaw in FortiMail is facing exploitation
feed.summary: Fortinet has issued a warning about a critical path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-104286) in its FortiMail platform that is actively being exploited. This zero-day flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files to the system, potentially granting full access to mail gateways, stored mail, credentials, and connected systems. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added this vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, urging users to apply workarounds, such as disabling identity-based encryption or restricting management interface access.

feed.title: Amazon to move US$8bn of chips off its books: ‘FT’
feed.summary: Amazon is reportedly exploring a deal to shift approximately US$8 billion worth of Nvidia Corp chips off its balance sheet. This move would involve transferring thousands of Grace Blackwell chips into a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside investors, allowing Amazon to continue using the hardware while adopting a more asset-light financing model. This elaborate financing strategy reflects the significant investments major tech providers are making in AI infrastructure.

feed.title: ON Semiconductor Analyst's 5 Key Takeaways from Synaptics Acquistion
